title: Epic
rule: Captions in an inflated heroic register: the errand a quest, the cupboard a vault, the question a summons.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

made: a storyboard sheet headed by a torn title slip 'THE QUEST OF THE BRASS KEY / an epic of Randolph station, in six cantos' with pen-drawn laurel sprigs; six cream storyboard boards titled 'CANTO I-VI' with event and time (4:09-4:11), each with a torn commentary slip pinned below

page 03's ENGRAVING PUPPETS reused (kit/build_page03.py): the AGENT is the Harper's Weekly 1863 telegraph operator (LoC cph.3c11072) cut at the joints and pinned with brass brads; the STRANGER the hatted woman of the 1867 Steinway Hall engraving (LoC cph.3c32079), in cantos II-IV seen only THROUGH the window glass on the platform side (as page 45, print 2): head and bust cropped at the sill (the sash's meeting rail), masked to the two upper panes so the sash bars and frame stay in front of her, tone-lifted toward the glass and multiplied under the plate's own glass hatching; his table and the TICKET OFFICE window cut from the 1863 plate; memo, clock (4:09 / 4:10), cupboard (closed / open with the key on its hook tagged SERVICE) and SERVICE door drawn in the shared pen hand
six commentary slips in an inflated heroic register (invocation, epithets, 'lo!'), written for this page; the four canon lines verbatim in cut-paper balloons
layout measured from the slips so no heading touches a slip; the LoC sheet softened 1.8 px for the JPEG budget

repair (batch 5): canto headings now read 'CANTO N' and the time only; the canto II balloon moved right of the window so her head and hat show; canto III re-laid (clock, agent, balloon in the office; the window and her bust behind its glass at the right); canto IV she has turned to face right (west) and is half past the right edge of the pane

self_check.register: heroic/epic: invocation of the Muse, epithets (keeper of the hours, the far-travelled one), the errand a Quest, the cupboard the Vault, the question a summons, the clock the Orb of the Hours, the memo the sacred scroll, the SERVICE tag a rune, 'lo!', 'Here ends the Quest'
captions: Sing, O Muse, of the Agent of Randolph, keeper of the hours! Upon his desk the sacred scroll laid its command: at the fourth hour and the quarter the Door of SERVICE must be opened, and the Key lies in the Vault. Then rose the hero and set forth upon the Quest.
But lo! as he strode the great hall, a stranger from far lands cried a summons through the gate of glass.
And he lifted his eyes to the mighty Orb of the Hours, that never sleeps, and gave answer.
Then the far-travelled one gave thanks, as wayfarers have ever done, and passed from the gate into the west.
Onward to the Vault strode the hero and flung wide its door: lo, the Brass Key, bearing the rune SERVICE!

But the jealous gods had stolen his purpose from his breast. Pencil to chin he stood before the open Vault, and spoke unto his own heart. So the Key hung on, unclaimed; the Door of SERVICE stayed sealed. Here ends the Quest.
